references.text: The same command to remove leaven for seven days and the threat of being cut off from Israel for anyone who eats leavened bread.
Repeats the command that unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days, and that no leaven shall be found among the Israelites.
Similar wording about being cut off from the people for anyone who breaks the Lord's command regarding purity.
The same penalty of being cut off from the people applies to anyone who neglects the Passover command.
The same law applies both to the native-born and to the foreigner living among the Israelites.
The command to eat unleavened bread for seven days during the Passover festival, and that no leaven shall be found in the land.
Paul uses leaven as a symbol of sin and urges the church to cleanse out the old leaven and celebrate the feast with unleavened bread.
This reference elaborates on the Passover law by linking the requirement for the absence of leaven directly to the timing of the sacrifice and purity requirements.
This reference explains the theological reason behind the prohibition of leaven: it is a memorial of God's swift deliverance from Egypt.
This reference confirms the appointed time (the month of Abib) and repeats the command for unleavened bread as a central part of the festival celebration.
This reference confirms the name of the month (Aviv) and restates the festival command, emphasizing the continuity of the law.
This reference elaborates on the structure of the seven days of Passover by distinguishing between eating unleavened bread and the rest observed on the seventh day.
